title: AI tools for support: Copilot and AI ticket triage
summary: Meet Microsoft Copilot and its support-focused variants, and learn how to use AI to triage, summarize, prioritize, and reply to tickets faster while always verifying the output before you trust it.
objectives: Describe Microsoft Copilot and its key variants (Copilot chat, Copilot in Intune, Microsoft Security Copilot)
Use AI to summarize long ticket threads and turn vague user reports into structured troubleshooting steps
Write prompts that classify, prioritize, and route tickets and suggest likely causes and KB articles
Draft clear, professional user-facing replies with AI and edit them for accuracy and tone
Use Copilot in Intune to ask natural-language questions about your tenant's devices and policies
Apply a verify-before-trust discipline: check facts, protect PII, and never send AI replies blindly

quiz.q: Which Copilot variant is designed specifically to answer natural-language questions about your tenant's devices, policies, and apps?
quiz.why: Copilot in Intune is embedded in the Intune admin center and can answer questions about your managed devices, configuration, and policies using your tenant's own data.

quiz.q: A user files a vague ticket: 'My laptop is broken.' What is a good first use of AI here?
options: Immediately email them a fix you guessed
Ask AI to turn the report into structured clarifying questions and likely troubleshooting steps
quiz.why: AI is excellent at converting a vague report into a structured set of clarifying questions and a ranked list of likely causes, which speeds up triage without guessing.

quiz.q: Why should you never send an AI-drafted reply to a user without reviewing it?
options: AI replies are always too short
It might contain inaccurate facts, the wrong tone, or leaked details, and AI can hallucinate
quiz.why: AI can hallucinate facts, miss context, use the wrong tone, or echo sensitive data. You are accountable for what you send, so always read and correct it first.

quiz.q: Which is the security-operations focused Copilot used by SOC and security teams?
quiz.why: Microsoft Security Copilot is the generative AI security product that helps analysts investigate incidents, summarize alerts, and respond to threats.

quiz.q: Give one example of sensitive information you must NOT paste into a public LLM when triaging a ticket.
quiz.answer: Passwords, access tokens, customer PII, or internal IP addresses and secrets.
quiz.why: Public LLMs may log or train on input, so credentials, PII, and confidential tenant data must never be pasted into them.

quiz.q: In one sentence, how does AI help you prioritize a flood of tickets?
quiz.answer: AI can classify each ticket by category and urgency and suggest a priority and routing queue, so you triage faster, but you confirm the calls yourself.
quiz.why: Classification and prioritization are pattern tasks AI does well, but the human owns the final routing and priority decision.

body_markdown:
## What is Microsoft Copilot?

**Microsoft Copilot** is Microsoft's family of generative AI assistants built into the tools you already use. For a support tech, three variants matter most. **Copilot chat** (the general assistant in Microsoft 365, Edge, and Windows) helps you summarize, draft, and reason in plain language. **Copilot in Intune** is embedded in the Intune admin center and can answer natural-language questions about *your tenant's own* devices, policies, and apps. **Microsoft Security Copilot** is the security-operations assistant that helps SOC teams investigate incidents and alerts.

You will also meet general LLM assistants (the public chatbots). They are powerful for drafting and explaining, but they do **not** see your tenant data and they carry real privacy and accuracy risks.

## Triage: from chaos to a sorted queue

Tier 1 lives in the ticket queue. AI shines at the boring-but-critical triage work: reading a long thread, pulling out what matters, and suggesting where the ticket should go. Use it to **summarize** a 40-message email chain into three lines, **classify** a ticket by category, and **suggest a priority** and routing queue.

```text
Summarize this ticket thread in 4 bullets: the user's core problem,
what has already been tried, the current state, and the single most
likely next step. Then suggest a category (hardware / network /
identity / app) and a priority (P1-P4) with a one-line reason.
[paste thread]
```

## Turning a vague report into structured steps

Users rarely write good tickets. "My laptop is broken" is a starting point, not a diagnosis. Ask AI to convert the vague report into structured clarifying questions and a ranked list of likely causes plus the first diagnostic step for each.

```text
A user reports: "Outlook keeps asking me to sign in and then fails."
List the 5 most likely causes ranked by probability for a Microsoft
365 / Entra ID managed device, the one question I should ask the user
for each, and the first thing I should check. Keep it concise.
```

## Drafting replies and finding KB articles

AI is great at drafting a **clear, friendly, professional reply** at the right reading level. It can also suggest which **KB articles** likely apply. But you are accountable for what you send.

```text
Draft a short, friendly reply telling the user we have reset their
password, they must change it at next sign-in, and to call us if MFA
fails. Plain English, no jargon, under 80 words.
```

## Copilot in Intune: ask your tenant

Inside the Intune admin center you can ask Copilot questions about real devices.

```text
1. Go to https://intune.microsoft.com
2. Open a device or a policy blade
3. Open the Copilot pane
4. Ask: "Why is this device showing as non-compliant?"
   or "Which policies are assigned to this device?"
```

This grounds the answer in *your* data rather than the open internet, which makes it far more trustworthy than a public chatbot for tenant questions.

## Verify before you trust

This is the rule that separates a pro from a liability. **AI can hallucinate** — it can invent facts, KB numbers, and error-code meanings with total confidence. So: never send an AI reply blindly; read every line and confirm the facts. Watch for **PII and secrets** — never paste passwords, tokens, customer data, or internal IPs into a public LLM. Cross-check any technical claim against **official Microsoft docs**. AI gives you a faster first draft and a set of hypotheses, not the final word.

## Your task

Take one real (or realistic) messy ticket thread. Use an AI assistant to (1) summarize it in four bullets, (2) suggest a category and priority, and (3) draft a user reply. Then edit the reply for accuracy and tone, and write one sentence on what you had to correct.

slides.narration: Welcome back. This lesson is where modern support gets genuinely exciting. We're going to look at Microsoft Copilot and how AI can help you tear through your ticket queue, summarizing long threads, sorting and prioritizing, and drafting clean replies. But there's a golden rule running through all of it: AI gives you a fast first draft, never the final word. You verify before you trust. Let's dig in.

slides.title: What is Microsoft Copilot?
bullets: A family of generative AI assistants built into Microsoft tools.
Copilot chat: general assistant in Microsoft 365, Edge, Windows.
Copilot in Intune: answers questions about your tenant's devices.
Microsoft Security Copilot: for security operations teams.
slides.narration: So what is Microsoft Copilot? It's not one thing, it's a family of generative AI assistants baked into the tools you already use. Three matter most to you. Copilot chat is the general assistant for summarizing and drafting. Copilot in Intune lives in the admin center and answers questions about your own tenant's devices and policies. And Microsoft Security Copilot is the one security teams use to investigate incidents. Different tools, different jobs.

slides.title: Public LLMs vs tenant-grounded AI
bullets: Public chatbots are great for drafting and explaining.
They do NOT see your tenant data.
They carry privacy and accuracy risks.
Copilot in Intune is grounded in your real data, so trust it more.
slides.narration: You'll also use general public chatbots, and they're brilliant for drafting and explaining concepts. But understand the difference: a public LLM cannot see your tenant. It's guessing from general knowledge, and it carries real privacy risk if you paste sensitive data in. Copilot in Intune, by contrast, is grounded in your actual device and policy data, so for tenant-specific questions it's far more trustworthy. Pick the right tool for the question.

Ask it to classify the ticket by category and suggest a priority and which queue it should route to. Here's a sample prompt you can reuse. The AI does the sorting grunt-work in seconds, but you confirm the final category and priority. It suggests, you decide.
